For every N=n+1 take Q uniform on {false,true}^N, p=1/2, M_i(z)=bit(z_i), H=1, D=0 and exceptional=0. The empty graph is a genuine collection-dependency graph: each pair (z_i,bit(z_i)) is a function of its own independent coordinate, so arbitrary predicates of disjoint collections are independent. For prescribed patterns on disjoint A,B the joint probability is 2^(-|A|-|B|), proving the factorization at every N. The AMR is 1, the nonempty-arm Hájek estimate is 1 and empty arms have total probability 2^(1-N)→0. scratch/Check.lean checks the Bernoulli law for every N and the uniform bound; scratch/verify.py verifies collection factorization and completed-estimator error for N=1,...,6, with a general counting argument recorded in scratch/finite-checks.json.
